title: Cash & Cash Equivalents
description: Understand cash classifications, cash equivalents, restricted cash, bank reconciliations and financial statement presentation.
html:
Cash & Cash Equivalents

Cash is one of the most liquid assets on the balance sheet. For CPA Exam purposes, you should be able to determine which items qualify as cash or cash equivalents, identify restricted cash, and understand basic bank reconciliation concepts.

1. What Is Included in Cash?

Cash generally includes amounts that are immediately available for use in paying current obligations.

Common examples include:

  • Currency and coins
  • Demand deposits in checking accounts
  • Savings accounts available for withdrawal
  • Undeposited customer checks
  • Cashier's checks and money orders held by the company

2. Cash Equivalents

Cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid investments that are readily convertible to known amounts of cash and have an insignificant risk of changes in value.

Original maturity: Generally three months or less

The maturity test is generally based on the investment's original maturity when acquired by the company, not simply how much time remains until maturity at the reporting date.

Example

A company purchases a U.S. Treasury bill when it has two months remaining until maturity.

Assuming the other cash-equivalent criteria are met, the Treasury bill may qualify as a cash equivalent.

However, an investment originally purchased with a one-year maturity does not become a cash equivalent merely because only two months remain before maturity.

3. Items That Are Generally Not Cash

  • Postdated checks received from customers
  • Employee advances
  • IOUs
  • Stale or uncollectible checks
  • Certificates of deposit or investments that do not meet the cash-equivalent requirements

4. Restricted Cash

Cash may be restricted for a specific purpose and therefore unavailable for general operations.

Examples can include cash restricted for debt repayment, construction, contractual requirements, or other designated purposes.

Restricted cash is still cash, but the nature and duration of the restriction affect its financial statement classification, presentation, and disclosure.

For example, cash restricted for a long-term purpose, such as construction of a noncurrent asset or repayment of long-term debt, generally should not be classified with unrestricted current cash.

5. Bank Reconciliations

A bank reconciliation explains differences between the cash balance reported by the bank and the cash balance recorded in the company's accounting records.

Common Bank-Side Adjustments

  • Deposits in transit
  • Outstanding checks
  • Bank errors

Common Book-Side Adjustments

  • Bank service charges
  • NSF customer checks
  • Interest earned
  • Electronic collections or payments not yet recorded
  • Errors made in the company's accounting records
Adjusted Bank Balance = Adjusted Book Balance

Bank Reconciliation Example

Bank statement balance: $52,000

Add deposits in transit: $6,000

Subtract outstanding checks: $8,000

$52,000 + $6,000 − $8,000 = $50,000 adjusted cash balance

6. CPA Exam Focus

  • Know what qualifies as cash.
  • Apply the cash-equivalent maturity concept correctly.
  • Distinguish restricted cash from unrestricted cash.
  • Know whether a reconciliation item adjusts the bank side or the book side.
  • Remember that book-side reconciling items generally require accounting entries.

quiz.prompt: Which investment is most likely to qualify as a cash equivalent?

choices.text: A bond purchased with five years remaining until maturity
A Treasury bill purchased when it has two months remaining until maturity
Common stock expected to be sold within three months
A one-year certificate of deposit purchased eleven months ago

quiz.explanation: Cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid investments that are readily convertible to known amounts of cash and generally have an original maturity of three months or less when acquired. A Treasury bill purchased with two months remaining until maturity can meet that requirement.
